Description

We are seeking an AI Engineer
to design, build, and ship the AI-powered features that sit at the heart of the Lexapar platform. A core part of this role is building and owning the model harnesses that let the team develop, test, and compare AI systems with confidence with the evaluation suites, agentic/tool-use scaffolding, and production instrumentation that turn frontier model capability into reliable, shippable features. You will work closely with product, engineering, and legal domain experts to translate real legal workflows into AI-driven product experiences that meet the accuracy and reliability bar the profession demands.

What you’ll do

Model Harness Development: Build and maintain the harnesses that power model development at Lexapar, evaluation harnesses, agentic/tool-use scaffolding, prompt and context test beds, and regression suites that let the team run, compare, and validate models quickly and reproducibly. This is a major, ongoing focus of the role.
AI Feature Development: Design, build, and ship production features powered by LLMs and other AI models, from prototype to scaled, reliable functionality within the Lexapar platform.
Retrieval & Agentic Systems: Build and optimize RAG pipelines, tool-use/agentic workflows, and orchestration layers that let models reason over legal documents and take multi-step actions reliably.
Prompt & System Design: Design and iterate on prompts, context strategies, and system architecture to maximize accuracy, consistency, and cost-efficiency across use cases.
Model Integration & Evaluation: Integrate best-fit foundation models (proprietary and open-source) into the product through the team’s harnesses, running structured evals to measure output quality, latency, and cost trade-offs before and after release.
Production Reliability: Own the AI layer end-to-end in production, monitoring, guardrails, fallback logic, and observability to ensure outputs meet legal-grade accuracy and reliability standards.
Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with product, engineering, and legal domain experts to translate ambiguous workflow problems into well-scoped AI features, and to validate outputs against professional legal standards.

Qualifications

AI/LLM Experience: 3+ years of hands-on experience building applications or systems on top of LLMs and other AI models, in production settings.
Harness & Eval Building: Demonstrated experience building model harnesses or evaluation infrastructure: test suites, benchmark runners, or scaffolding used to systematically compare and validate model behavior.
Applied Systems Skill: Practical experience with retrieval-augmented generation, agentic/tool-use frameworks, prompt engineering, and orchestration across multiple models or providers.
Software Engineering Fundamentals: Strong backend/software engineering skills, with the ability to design and ship robust, well-tested production systems.
Evaluation Mindset: Comfortable designing evals and quality checks to validate AI output before and after shipping, and iterating based on real usage data.
Model Fluency: Working knowledge of the LLM landscape including API-based and open-source models, fine-tuning vs. prompting trade-offs.
Autonomy & Drive: Comfortable operating with a high degree of independence, initiative, and speed in a fast-moving, resource-lean environment.
Domain Context (Preferred): Interest in or exposure to legal technology, document-heavy workflows, or other high-stakes, regulated application areas.

The opportunity to build the AI-powered features and infrastructure at the core of a category-defining legal tech product, with direct visibility into company strategy.
A collaborative environment working alongside experienced technologists and legal professionals who speak your language.
Competitive compensation, commensurate with experience.

engineer. You need strong applied AI engineering and practical cybersecurity ability to understand

security tasks, interpret evidence and diagnose unsuccessful runs.

cancellation and execution traces.

- Integrate security tools and enforce permissions, approval steps, scope boundaries, execution limits and

stop controls in application code. Handle credentials, untrusted target/tool content and isolated

execution safely.

- Integrate hosted and open-weight models while preserving application-owned state, evidence and tool

contracts. Adapt prompts and integrations where needed and test for regressions.

- Capture task context, tool actions/results, failures, versions, reviewer corrections, timing and cost in a

form the data/model engineer can use for reviewed datasets and evaluations.

- Jointly define versioned trace and tool interfaces, evaluation criteria and release checks with the

data/model engineer and cybersecurity specialists. Security specialists review domain labels and

validate findings.

- Support observable, recoverable workloads and deployment, including private or self-hosted

environments; investigate concurrency, reliability and resource-use problems with the engineering

team.

- Work with security specialists and the data/model engineer to test task success, evidence quality, false

positives, latency and cost, and release improvements with regression checks and rollback.

SecNinjaz Technologies LLP 1

- Around two years of hands-on development experience; strong Python, APIs, Git, debugging and

automated testing.

- A working AI/LLM application or agent with tool integration, state, meaningful tests and failure handling.

- Practical understanding of model limitations, prompting, structured outputs, retrieval and evaluation.

- Conceptual understanding of training versus inference and of reinforcement-learning fundamentals:

environments, actions, rewards and evaluation. An implemented RL project is welcome but not required

for this role.

- Demonstrated practical cybersecurity ability:
reason about authentication, authorization, trust
boundaries and common web/API or code weaknesses; interpret tool output, reproduce and validate a
finding, reject a false positive and verify a fix in a controlled environment.
- Comfort with Linux, HTTP/APIs, logs and application deployment, and explaining technical decisions to
teammates.
Relevant professional work, labs, research and personal projects can demonstrate these skills.
Good to have

- Docker, CI/CD, queues, monitoring or production reliability experience.

- Private inference, open-weight model serving or inference performance work.

- Deeper security-tool integration, detection engineering or security research.

- Fine-tuning or implemented RL experiments.

- Deliver a tested security workflow with useful traces and independently validated outcomes.

- Demonstrate recovery from a failed run and a control, enforced in application code, that blocks an

unapproved action.

- Run the workflow through two model integrations with retained application state and regression checks;

supply usable trace records to the data/evaluation pipeline.

Selection process

A project discussion and a short practical exercise using a supplied lab or sanitized security case. You will

interpret tool outputs that include a false positive, diagnose a failed agent run, implement a recovery or

permission-control improvement, and define a trustworthy success check.

AI tools may be used; explain your contribution and be ready to debug your solution. Nothing is run
